feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete platforms, scope, and outcomes. It reads clearly overall, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some formatting/style inconsistencies that reduce polish.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic scope over time.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools add impact and credibility.  
- Strong alignment between headline, competencies, experience, and technical skills; the profile is coherent and well-positioned for digital platform leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; several themes/tools appear multiple times, making the CV longer than necessary.  
- Improve formatting consistency: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically uneven; bullet formatting in work entries is awkward; use either “AI-enabled” or “AI enabled” consistently; standardize commas around lists (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs no Oxford comma elsewhere).  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities, especially in recent consulting work. Few clear errors, but minor style/grammar edits would help: “Ranked among the top public universities...” is unnecessary filler, and “French (A2/Learning)” would read better as “French (A2, learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads broad and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and slightly tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems, governance models and content operations. Led enterprise website transformation for a 10,000+ page Drupal platform serving 3.5M annual page views, while building analytics, editorial, multimedia and AI-enabled discovery systems for mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct verbs like “modernizing,” “scaling,” or “leading.”
- Add 1–2 proof points from recent roles only, such as 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, or 50+ internal publishers.
- Keep the subtitle and intro distinct: use the subtitle for positioning, and the intro for evidence and scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” closely repeat Core Competencies.
- “Multimedia production” is already emphasized elsewhere; keep it only if central to target roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording for consistency: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Consider replacing “website” with “web” for a more senior, enterprise tone.
- Change “content experiences” to “content discovery” or “user experiences” for clearer meaning.
- If space allows, prioritize the most current differentiators first: AI-enabled search, enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” already appear in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more additive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize distinct value not already stated in experience bullets: user problem solved, platform/format, and visible result or purpose.
- Standardize style: use consistent verb tense, serial commas, and “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot.”
- Consider this tighter wording: “AI Hybrid Search: Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current consultant and NACo role bullets.
- If space is tight, keep only the most differentiated 1–2 projects or add outcomes not mentioned elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact recent engagement. Tighten around 3–4 outcomes-focused themes and avoid repeating NACo achievements already covered in prior roles and Recent Projects.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, Drupal platform improvements, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper impact statements, e.g.:
- “Designed and improved cross-channel workflows, governance, and analytics to support coordinated web, email, social, and multimedia communications.”
- “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search strategy, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and user-facing discovery experience.”
- Replace generic phrases like “deliver technical troubleshooting” with stronger verbs and scale/outcomes where possible: launched, streamlined, reduced, increased, supported X teams/users/pages.
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of sites/modules launched, publishing time reduced, engagement gains, or adoption by teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording overlaps with prior NACo entries on governance, analytics, Drupal, and cross-channel operations.
- Microsite and AI search bullets also duplicate Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level unless you add new results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: for email/social, include open rates, audience growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available.
- Tighten phrasing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video/programming language overlaps with earlier NACo roles; emphasize studio buildout and organizational scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and team/process coordination at that stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, supporting NACo’s advocacy messaging and cross-channel editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership if accurate: “Improved editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- “Produced weekly video updates” echoes the 2015–2018 role; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing, not originating.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad labels with sharper, executive-level wording tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social & video)
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy & campaign planning
- Use “transformation,” “operations,” and “campaign planning” to sound more outcome-oriented than “leadership” or “planning” alone.
- Keep parallel structure: noun phrase + scope; avoid mixing abstract traits with channels.
- If space allows elsewhere, move proof points like “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views” into experience only, not skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” repeats the header’s “advocacy messaging” and core competencies’ “Policy & advocacy communication.”
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with both the header and Core Competencies; the revised version is more specific.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization, AI search, and systems execution.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal/CMS modernization first since it aligns most directly with the most recent roles.
- Use parallel phrasing and trim weaker wording: change “AI-enabled search experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery.”
- If space allows, add one scope cue from recent work: “enterprise Drupal environments” or “large public-facing web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills more strategic/capability-based and leave full tool inventory below.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Workflow & systems architecture.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for your most recent leadership work, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Tighten it to emphasize decision support, measurement, and optimization outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Rename/refocus as: **Analytics, Reporting & Performance Optimization**
- Replace the list with: **GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • Web, SEO, and conversion performance analysis**
- If space allows, make it more outcome-oriented: **Analytics stack development, KPI design, executive reporting, and performance analysis across web and search channels**
- Keep only the strongest, current tools; order by strategic relevance, not alphabetically

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with **Core Competencies: Data analytics & reporting**; use this section for specific tools/methods, not generic analytics language
- Avoid repeating the exact GA4/Clarity/Power BI/Looker Studio/BigQuery list elsewhere unless tied to a measurable achievement in recent NACo roles

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with stronger evidence already shown in recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, current capabilities and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with more senior, outcome-oriented wording: “Broadcast video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera direction,” “Studio build-out and operations.”
- Reorder by strength/relevance to recent roles: Hybrid/virtual event production, livestream production, studio operations, video production/editing, PTZ systems.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Hybrid and virtual event production • Livestream production • Broadcast video production and editing • Studio operations and build-out • PTZ camera systems”
- If accurate, add scale or complexity elsewhere in the CV rather than here (e.g., number of events, recurring programs, in-house studio launch).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; keep one broader and one more specific.
- “Studio operations” and “video production and editing” are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid expanding this into a long list.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a duplicate of “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills and misses the chance to signal depth or recency. Make it more selective and weighted toward platforms tied to recent, high-impact work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise CMS migration, 10,000+ pages) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put Drupal first and add a brief qualifier only where it reinforces recent impact; keep the rest clean to avoid overloading a skills section.
- If space allows, group by strength: Advanced: Drupal, WordPress | Working knowledge: SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it has not featured meaningfully in recent roles; it is less central than your enterprise CMS work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps heavily with Topline Skills [2]; avoid repeating the exact same list in both places.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t add that phrase here unless you remove it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Replace with a tighter, grouped list: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version-specific labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; they add little value.
- If accurate, add one brief qualifier for impact/context, e.g., “for Drupal/CMS builds, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “Workflow automation” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider keeping the detailed tools here and shortening the Topline Skills version to avoid repeating the same technologies twice.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already present in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” or “Automation, PM & Collaboration Systems.”
- Group tools by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Drop one lower-value or older-feeling tool if space is tight; Basecamp or Trello are the easiest cuts unless central to recent work.
- If possible, tie this category to impact elsewhere in the CV by adding a qualifier such as “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation” in a summary/skills section rather than here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” and “editorial workflow design” already appear in Core Competencies.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the scale/strategic email work shown in recent NACo roles. Strengthen it by signaling CRM/email automation capability without repeating newsletter details already covered in experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Audience segmentation • Journey automation**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier instead of more tools: **list management**, **template deployment**, or **performance reporting**
- Keep platform names first; avoid slash-heavy phrasing if space allows: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Don’t restate “newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in recent work experience.
- Be careful adding “analytics/reporting” since GA4, Power BI, and Looker Studio are already covered elsewhere.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools for the recent NACo leadership work, but this item overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it to emphasize analysis/optimization capabilities rather than repeating platforms already highlighted elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- Put the most strategic/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- If space allows elsewhere, replace generic terms with outcomes-linked phrasing, e.g., **KPI dashboarding** instead of **Dashboarding**, and **SEO analysis** instead of **SEO**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider keeping detailed tools here and trimming the topline version to broader capabilities only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating all five in multiple sections unless needed for ATS.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to what was first built or launched during this earlier period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social media and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, cadence/audience for weekly videos, or any growth/efficiency results.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce soft language like “supporting,” “contributed,” and “high-impact”; use stronger verbs such as “helped launch,” “produced,” “streamlined,” “trained,” or “supervised.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social media and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as the launch/build phase if true.
- Avoid repeating generic workflow language already used heavily in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital work. Tighten it to emphasize the innovation/research scope plus the distinctive launch accomplishment.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground outcomes and ownership: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; translated findings into digital and multimedia content for member audiences.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more resume-friendly: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If you can, add scale or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Remove filler like “contributed to” where you had direct responsibility; use stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item lighter on generic multimedia language.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream themes here unless this role truly centered on them.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep workflow/production capabilities in experience or topline skills.

Suggested edit:
